children: Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar, but may be weighed down by rising Middle East tensions that could support safe-haven demand for the greenback. Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants conducted a missile attack on Saudi Arabia's international airport that killed at least 12 people and injured hundreds more on Saturday. "We expect the Houthis to continue their attacks on Saudi Arabian energy assets," CBA's Global Economic & Markets Research team says in a research report. This should support gains in the dollar, the team adds. The U.S. dollar is down 0.1% at 1,339.10 won, but is little changed at 1.2802 Singapore dollars, while the Australian dollar is flat at US$0.6983, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
